content.value_statement: Animation can fail when playback is not deterministic or visible poses are unclear. This skill defines keyframes, runtime rules, and diagnostics for reliable HyperFrames motion.
actual_capabilities: Defines visible poses and final states for 2D and 3D animation.
Selects GSAP, CSS, Anime.js, WAAPI, FLIP, SVG, or WebGL mechanisms.
Provides seek-safe runtime rules for deterministic rendering.
Guides keyframe timing, path travel, text motion, masks, and depth.
Recommends focused HyperFrames diagnostics and snapshot checks.
limitations: Does not create broad scene strategy, brand direction, or media plans.
Does not provide complete HyperFrames CLI documentation.
Requires an existing HyperFrames composition and supported animation runtime.
Does not guarantee visual quality without reviewing rendered snapshots.

use_cases.title: Refine product motion
use_cases.description: Define visible UI state changes with deterministic timing and a verified final state.

use_cases.title: Implement animation runtime
use_cases.description: Choose a seek-safe GSAP, CSS, Anime.js, or WAAPI implementation pattern.

use_cases.title: Verify rendered motion
use_cases.description: Plan targeted diagnostics and snapshots for paths, masks, text, and 3D motion.

prompt_templates.title: Create a simple keyframe plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a seek-safe keyframe plan for a card that moves right, settles, and remains visible at the final frame.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an animation mechanism
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the smallest mechanism for one element moving between two layout boxes. Explain the visible poses and final state.

prompt_templates.title: Make a GSAP timeline seek-safe
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this HyperFrames GSAP animation. List changes needed for synchronous construction, registration, finite playback, and seek-safe rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Design proof for 3D motion
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan keyframes and diagnostics for a WebGL object that crosses depth layers. Include camera poses, proof times, and snapshot checks.

output_examples.input: A notification card should enter, pause for reading, then settle in its final position.
output: Poses: offscreen start, readable arrival, final settled state.
Use a finite registered timeline with an explicit final hold.
Capture snapshots at arrival, final-minus-hold, and exact final.

output_examples.input: A logo path should draw on before the final lockup.
output: Use stroke drawing for the visible route.
Define a blank start, a clear partial draw, a completed logo, and a final hold.
Verify the partial and completed states with focused snapshots.

best_practices: Name the moving subject and every visible proof pose before implementation.
Use finite, synchronous, registered animation instances for render-critical motion.
Verify first frame, proof poses, final-minus-hold, and exact final with rendered snapshots.
anti_patterns: Do not use timers, unseeded randomness, or uncontrolled playback for render-critical motion.
Do not replace continuous motion with a crossfade unless replacement is the intended effect.
Do not treat helper overlays or logs as proof when the rendered frame is incorrect.

faq.question: What does seek-safe mean?
faq.answer: The animation can render a requested time deterministically without depending on prior playback.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a HyperFrames composition needs specific, verifiable keyframe motion.

faq.question: Does it support GSAP?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes rules for paused, finite, registered GSAP timelines.

faq.question: Can it help with SVG and WebGL motion?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers stroke drawing, shape interpolation, camera motion, and shader-related keyframes.

faq.question: How should I verify an animation?
faq.answer: Run focused HyperFrames diagnostics and capture snapshots at meaningful proof times.

faq.question: Does it design a complete video scene?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on animation mechanics, not broad scene planning or brand design.
